content: Choline magnesium trisalicylate is a medication prescribed to alleviate pain, tenderness, inflammation (swelling), and stiffness associated with arthritis and painful shoulder conditions. It is also used to reduce pain and lower fever. This drug belongs to a class of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) known as salicylates. It works by inhibiting the production of substances in the body that cause pain, fever, and inflammation. Choline magnesium trisalicylate is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken one to three times daily. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to take the medication at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, and do not take more or less than prescribed or take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking choline magnesium trisalicylate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, aspirin, choline salicylate (Arthropan), diflunisal (Dolobid), magnesium salicylate (Doan's, others), salsalate (Argesic, Disalcid, Salgesic), or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Be sure to mention specific drugs such as acetazolamide (Diamox), antacids, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), dichlorphenamide (Daranide), insulin, oral diabetes medications (e.g., glimepiride, glipizide, glyburide), gout medications (e.g., probenecid, sulfinpyrazone), methotrexate, oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, prednisone), other salicylate pain relievers (e.g., aspirin, choline salicylate), phenytoin, and valproic acid. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had stomach problems such as ulcers, or kidney or liver disease. Note that this medication should not be given to children or teenagers with chickenpox or the flu due to the risk of Reye syndrome, a rare but serious condition. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while taking this medication, as alcohol can exacerbate its side effects. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Choline magnesium trisalicylate may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they persist or worsen: upset stomach, vomiting, heartburn, diarrhea, constipation, stomach pain, headache, lightheadedness, dizziness, drowsiness, or lack of energy. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience ringing in the ears, hearing loss, black or tarry stools, red blood in stools, bloody vomit, or vomit that resembles coffee grounds. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Symptoms of overdose may include headache, dizziness, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, confusion, drowsiness, sweating, vomiting, diarrhea, and rapid breathing. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order specific lab tests to monitor your body's response to this medication. Before undergoing any laboratory tests, inform your doctor and the laboratory personnel that you are taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription.
